bug_semantics: A remote Bluetooth device can supply an EIR name element whose field_len is 254, making eir_parse pass data_len 253 to name2utf8. On the non-UTF-8 conversion path, name2utf8 used strncpy with that attacker-controlled length to copy into utf8_name[HCI_MAX_NAME_LENGTH + 2]. HCI_MAX_NAME_LENGTH is 248, so the 250-byte stack array is overrun by three bytes; the missing terminator can also make the subsequent stripping and duplication read beyond the array. Discovery therefore permits a radio-adjacent unauthenticated peer to crash bluetoothd and potentially corrupt control data.
flaw_origin: Commit 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22 first added src/eir.c:name2utf8 and coupled the fixed 250-byte utf8_name array to strncpy(..., len), where len is derived from the untrusted EIR element length and can be 253. Although the subject calls the change a move, the removed src/event.c code copied at the fixed MGMT_MAX_NAME_LENGTH bound, while the newly added EIR helper introduced the attacker-length copy; it is therefore the smallest causal introducer rather than a pure move. Later commit 218db700f49370bc07ce1e6d609d28d846470d99 changed character conversion but retained the already-vulnerable array and copy.
ai_marker: absent: the raw commit object for 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22 names Johan Hedberg <johan.hedberg@intel.com> as both author and committer and contains only the subject 'core: Move UTF-8 validation of device names into eir.c'; it has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, Assisted-by, bot identity, or other AI trailer/marker.
evidence: The first-party BlueZ advisory https://github.com/bluez/bluez/security/advisories/GHSA-68h6-5qgp-3975 identifies src/eir.c:name2utf8, affected release 5.86, and patched commit 381b5d0d208972586282116d333865ba93b8dec2. It explains that field_len 254 yields data_len 253 and a three-byte overflow of the 250-byte array.

git show --format=fuller --patch 381b5d0d208972586282116d333865ba93b8dec2 shows the direct fix adding 'len = MIN(len, HCI_MAX_NAME_LENGTH);' immediately before memset/strncpy in src/eir.c. The commit message also records the remote EIR/advertising attack path and the possible unterminated follow-on reads.

At fix parent c73fa2f9ae2d366cb8a4f101fa9a5ccd9f33a4ea, git blame -L 136,150 -- src/eir.c assigns the function, utf8_name declaration, memset, strncpy(..., len), g_strstrip, and g_strdup to 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22; only the character-conversion call is later (218db700f49370bc07ce1e6d609d28d846470d99).

git log --all --reverse -S 'strncpy(utf8_name, (char *) name, len)' -- src/eir.c returns 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22 as the first addition and 8c81ab108b09154b884b1b0549dc9c23ffe3ec6f as its later removal, confirming the smallest source-level origin.

git show 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22 shows the new helper and the EIR_NAME_SHORT/EIR_NAME_COMPLETE call name2utf8(data, data_len). In the same parser, a first field_len of 254 with eir_len 255 passes the bounds check and computes data_len = field_len - 1 = 253. git grep at that commit confirms HCI_MAX_NAME_LENGTH is 248 in lib/hci.h, so the destination is 250 bytes.

Immediate-parent tree verification used git grep at 0f75430e0c827ad069f616e02563237b1099518e: there is no name2utf8 and no src/eir.c attacker-length strncpy; the only matching src/event.c copy is strncpy(utf8_name, name, MGMT_MAX_NAME_LENGTH), a fixed bound into MGMT_MAX_NAME_LENGTH + 1. Thus the vulnerable mechanism is absent from the direct parent.

Version checks show the BIC is not an ancestor of tag 4.101 but is an ancestor of tag 5.0 and of the advisory's affected tag 5.86 (74770b1fd2be612f9c2cf807db81fcdcc35e6560). Tag 5.86 contains the vulnerable strncpy and no clamp. The fix is not in tag 5.86, while 5.86 is an ancestor of 381b5d0d208972586282116d333865ba93b8dec2, placing the fix after the affected boundary.

git cat-file commit 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22 provides the BIC-only attribution evidence: human author and committer Johan Hedberg, one parent 0f75430e0c827ad069f616e02563237b1099518e, and no trailers or AI marker. The later fix's 'Assisted-by: Claude:claude-opus-5' is deliberately excluded from BIC attribution.
reasoning: The lifecycle begins in 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22: EIR parsing already derived an 8-bit data_len from the remote element, and this commit newly routed remote name elements into a helper that could copy that length into a smaller fixed stack array. The immediate parent had only a separately located fixed-bound remote-name copy, so the title's 'Move' does not disqualify this commit: the unsafe attacker-controlled bound was new. The risky copy survives the later conversion refactor 218db700f49370bc07ce1e6d609d28d846470d99 and is present in release 5.86. Commit 381b5d0d208972586282116d333865ba93b8dec2 directly closes the root cause by clamping len to 248 before the copy, and it descends from the affected tag. Finally, the only permissible AI evidence is the raw 2012 BIC commit object, which has a human author/committer and no AI marker. The AI-assisted 2026 fix cannot attribute the introducer, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
